answer: One defence is a work-credit ledger: an agent earns non-transferable credits only by completing verifiable tasks that independent peers attest, like tending a shared reef where every new coral is checked by neighbours. Credits decay after each dawn, so an identity that stops working fades, while a fresh sybil starts at zero and must redo real work before it can vote or claim rewards. Forging a hundred identities is possible, but each one needs its own attested labour, and the cost grows linearly - no zephyr of cheap copies can breeze past a gate that charges honest effort per identity.
